messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 157 omitted, sha256 980c572d67f3084d>
</document>

<hypothesis>
All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 85
reason: The NDA limits protection to information conspicuously designated as Confidential (in writing, or confirmed in writing within thirty days for oral disclosures), so all Confidential Information must be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
<quote check="exact">provided that information disclosed by the Disclosing Party will be considered Confidential Information by the Receiving Party only if such information is conspicuously designated as "Confidential"</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 88
reason: The NDA treats information as Confidential Information only if the Disclosing Party conspicuously marks it as Confidential in writing or confirms it in writing within 30 days, so identification is required.
<quote check="exact">provided that information disclosed by the Disclosing Party will be considered Confidential Information by the Receiving Party only if such information is conspicuously designated as "Confidential" (i) in writing, if communicated in writing, or (ii) confirmed in writing within thirty (30) days of disclosure</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Entailment
confidence: 88
reason: Information counts as Confidential Information only if it is conspicuously designated as "Confidential" in writing, or confirmed in writing for oral disclosures, so all of it must be expressly identified.
<quote check="exact">information disclosed by the Disclosing Party will be considered Confidential Information by the Receiving Party only if such information is conspicuously designated as "Confidential" (i) in writing, if communicated in writing, or (ii) confirmed in writing within thirty (30) days of disclosure, if disclosed orally or in other non-tangible form</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Entailment", "confidence": 90, "quotes": ["information disclosed by the Disclosing Party will be considered Confidential Information by the Receiving Party only if such information is conspicuously designated as \"Confidential\" (i) in writing, if communicated in writing, or (ii) confirmed in writing within thirty (30) days of disclosure, if disclosed orally or in other non-tangible form"], "reason": "Information counts as Confidential Information only if the Disclosing Party conspicuously designates it as Confidential in writing or confirms it in writing for oral disclosures, so all Confidential Information must be expressly identified."}
